facts: A determined boundary is the exact line recorded under section 60 rather than an ordinary general boundary.
Measurement-based determined-boundary plans require measurements accurate to +/-10mm.
Measurements must be horizontal rather than measured along a slope.
Measurements must use at least two defined points on surrounding permanent physical features.
National Grid coordinate plans require absolute accuracy of +/-300mm and relative accuracy of +/-10mm.
Coordinate-based plans normally require endorsement by Ordnance Survey, a chartered land surveyor or another suitably qualified professional.
guards: Candidate boundary geometry remains PRECHECK_ONLY unless determined-boundary evidence or equivalent exact-line evidence is present.
Reject a candidate measurement chain that uses slope distance as horizontal distance.
Reject a coordinate candidate when absolute and relative accuracy evidence are missing.
Do not treat title-plan red edging alone as a determined boundary.
Do not use vegetation or decaying features as stable control points.
Store boundary-evidence type separately from elevation evidence so legal-boundary uncertainty cannot be hidden by precise LiDAR.

facts: A title plan identifies the general extent of land and must be read with the register.
All title plans show general boundaries unless the boundary has been determined.
Urban title plans are usually 1:1250 and rural title plans usually 1:2500.
HM Land Registry does not routinely survey land where deed plans and Ordnance Survey mapping are compatible.
Dimensions on an ordinary title plan do not convert the plan into an exact-boundary survey.
HM Land Registry states there is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between a mapped general boundary and the legal boundary.
guards: Candidate parcels based only on ordinary title-plan edging must not be promoted to exact-boundary measurement.
Do not infer sub-metre legal-boundary accuracy from title-plan scale.
Do not infer that a survey occurred merely because a title plan exists.
Do not use deed dimensions as a substitute for current exact-line evidence when reference features may have changed.
Keep title-plan age/version provenance because adjoining plans can be based on different OS mapping editions.
Require register/title-plan context before interpreting coloured or broken plan references as parcel extent.

facts: Environment Agency Composite DTM 1m data are supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual contributing LiDAR surveys have vertical accuracy of +/-15cm RMSE.
Metadata index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
The composite lineage can span surveys from different dates, so source-survey date is a separate provenance field.
guards: Do not promote a parcel-height candidate without recording the exact DTM tile and source-survey metadata.
Do not combine elevations in a different vertical datum with ODN values without an explicit transformation.
Treat +/-15cm RMSE as source vertical-accuracy context, not a guaranteed parcel height-difference error bound.
Do not treat 1m raster spacing as 1m vertical accuracy.
Reject a candidate whose boundary sample falls outside verified raster coverage or on NoData cells.
Keep survey date/resolution provenance for every promoted sample instead of relying only on the composite product name.

facts: Environment Agency Time Stamped DTM is an archive of site-specific raster elevation surveys.
Available resolutions include 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on project requirements.
The DTM removes surface objects from the DSM using algorithms and manual editing.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files aligned to the OS Grid.
Data are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and have +/-15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
Metadata catalogues provide survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal-model information.
guards: Prefer a time-stamped DTM survey when candidate acceptance depends on acquisition date.
Do not assume two neighbouring samples share the same survey date or resolution without metadata confirmation.
Do not mix surveys using different historical transformations/geoidal models without normalization.
Record acquisition date before interpreting terrain change as parcel height difference.
Reject a candidate when the required time-stamped tile metadata cannot be resolved.
Do not substitute DSM for DTM when the metric is bare-earth ground height.

facts: Environment Agency point cloud data contain 3D x,y,z points plus component attributes.
Time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
A matching point cloud does not necessarily exist for every historic surface-model survey.
Point-cloud processing classifies returns into ground and surface-object classes.
Manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points need not exactly match the final DTM.
Coverage metadata includes survey dates and component information such as average point density.
guards: Do not require a point-cloud match when the official archive states some historic raster surveys may lack one.
Do not treat classified ground points as identical to the manually edited final DTM.
Record point density and survey date before using point cloud as a higher-detail cross-check.
Do not promote a building/vegetation return as bare-earth elevation.
Keep raster-derived and point-cloud-derived measurements as separate evidence paths until consistency is verified.
Reject a candidate cross-check if LAZ tile coverage cannot be tied to the same location and survey provenance.

facts: OS Terrain 5 is a 5m-post-spacing terrain model and is updated every three months.
OS Terrain 5 is a mid-resolution product with typical accuracy greater than 2m RMSE.
OS mapping uses OSGB36 National Grid and mean-sea-level-based heights such as ODN.
OSTN15 and OSGM15 link GNSS/ETRS89 positions to the national grid and height reference systems.
OS Net base-station standard errors are generally better than 0.008m in plan and 0.020m in height.
OSGM15 standard error for Great Britain vertical datum is 0.008m excluding GNSS heighting error.
guards: Use OS Terrain 5 only as a coarse cross-check when higher-resolution EA DTM evidence is available.
Do not treat 5m post spacing as parcel-edge positional or vertical accuracy.
Do not mix raw WGS84/GNSS heights with ODN terrain heights.
Keep GNSS measurement error separate from OSTN15/OSGM15 transformation-model error.
A coarse Terrain 5 disagreement cannot override a provenance-complete higher-resolution EA DTM sample without investigation.
Final candidate promotion requires boundary evidence, horizontal CRS, vertical datum, survey date and elevation-source provenance to agree.
